column1: # freedesktop icon name -> Phosphor icon, per context.
# Only SEMANTIC names are mapped. Brand/app logos (brave-browser, slack, obsidian,
# google-chrome, ...) are deliberately absent: Phosphor has no logos, and replacing them
# with a generic glyph makes apps unidentifiable. index.theme Inherits=breeze-dark, so
# every unmapped name -- logos included -- resolves exactly as it does today.
# weight: the Phosphor weight, and it CARRIES MEANING.
#   fill    = solid   -> on / active / present / unread / connected / selected
#   regular = outline -> off / inactive / absent / read / disconnected / unselected
# Solid is the default look, so neutral objects (folder, printer, a text file) are `fill`.
# Outline is reserved for the negative half of a state pair, which is what makes the pair
# readable at a glance: starred vs non-starred, mail-unread vs mail-read, network-idle vs
# network-offline. The symbolic variant of a row uses that row's own weight, so a toggle
# keeps its state reading in GTK's small monochrome slots too.
# Zero is not mute: wireplumber's `off` state is volume 0 with the sink still live, and
# reusing the slash there would claim the sink is muted when nothing is holding it down.
# ── waybar module icons (consumed by CSS -gtk-icontheme(), not by any font) ─
# The tray drawer is its own state pair: outline while it is closed, solid once the items
# are out. Same fill/regular reading as every other toggle, so the handle needs no arrow.
# Four notification states, not three. bell-slash REGULAR is "silenced and nothing waiting";
# bell-slash FILL is "silenced but something IS waiting" -- the one case where you want to
# know the panel has something for you despite having asked not to be told.
# swaync's do-not-disturb row. A moon is the state's identity, not its value: the switch
# next to it carries on/off, so this stays one icon in both positions.
